title: Data Validation Library
prompt: Build reusable validators for common data formats and edge cases. Include a short README explaining inputs, expected behavior, normal cases, boundary cases, and how to run tests. Use synthetic examples only.
objective: Build reusable validators for common data formats and edge cases.

starter.code:
def valid_label?(value)
  value.is_a?(String) && !value.strip.empty?
end
# TODO: add format and boundary validators

expected_output: A Ruby program or library that meets the stated acceptance criteria. Verify it locally with the declared Ruby runtime and tests; CodeLeaf does not currently execute Ruby submissions in an isolated runner.
acceptance_criteria: The implementation covers the prompt and explains its input/output contract.
Normal input, boundary input, and at least one expected failure are handled and tested.
Code is organized into readable methods or objects where useful.
External input is validated; database operations use parameters; secrets and private data are not logged.
Run instructions and any limitations of static checks are documented.
hints: Write a small example before building the full workflow.
List empty, invalid, and boundary cases before coding.
Add automated tests and check that the expected output is reproducible.
grading_method: Static required-token smoke check only; it does not compile or execute Ruby and is not proof of correctness. This exercise remains draft until the course has a reviewed isolated runner or an explicit human-review workflow.
retry_policy: Allow revisions and retries. Course completion, idempotent progress, and platform-wide XP remain backend-controlled; this file contains no XP override.
status_note: Original learner task aligned to Ruby.pdf Section C; reference solution is kept in a repository-only file.
